speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the location and nature of your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the presence of bloody stools, I am concerned about a potential loss of blood flow to your intestines. Can you tell me if the pain is now more diffuse across your entire abdomen, and have you noticed any bloating or tenderness when I press on your stomach?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe pain out of proportion to your exam findings and the bloody stools, I strongly suspect acute mesenteric ischemia. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the abdomen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Angiography Abdomen: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, vomiting. Reports bloody loose bowel movements. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of migraine is clinically implausible given your recent heart attack and bloody stools; this is a surgical emergency. I am proceeding with the CT Angiography to confirm acute mesenteric ischemia immediately. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the abdomen

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
